paragraphs.text: # dsh-quit-idle-fix

Stop the DeepSeek Harness desktop app from warning that running tasks will be
interrupted when the o
nly thing left in the idle inbox is a system notice.
## The false alarm

The desktop quit check in `@deepseek-ai/dsh-desktop-host` counts **any** pending
`next-step` inbox m
essage as active work:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

But several host features queue purely informational messages with
`agent.inject()`, which does **no

t** wake an idle agent. When the approval
policy, working directory, plan mode, or a Cordis plugin c

hanges while a
conversation is idle, the notice waits in `next-step` forever. The quit check
then se

es a pending message and warns about interrupted work even though no
turn and no job is running.

This is an interaction bug in the harness itself (the official
`dsh-desktop-host` predicate plus the

official notice producers), not a
conflict caused by another installed plugin.
## What this plugin does

While an agent is `idle`, it consumes `next-step` messages whose
`source.kind` is one of:

- `user-approval` — approval policy changed
- `working-directory` — working directory changed or rec

overed
- `cordis-host-runner` — plugin add/remove/run result
- `plan-mode` — plan mode switched

The approval policy and working directory are already stated in the runtime
context, and plan mode i

s reflected in the prompt. Cordis plugin state can be
inspected again with the plugin tools. Running

agents are never touched, so a
notice queued mid-turn still reaches the next step. If a user turn i

s already
queued, the sweep backs off and lets that turn consume the notices.

It checks every 500 ms, does an immediate sweep on load, and keeps no state.
Agents with a queued `n
ext-turn` user message are skipped.

[代码示例省略，未执行]
Restart the app afterwards.
## Verify
[代码示例省略，未执行]

Then make sure no conversation is running and no background job is active,
and quit the desktop app.

The interrupt warning should no longer appear. If a
real job or turn is running, the warning still
appears — that is intended.
## Scope and limitations

- Desktop only. The web profile has no quit-confirmation dialog.
- Only the four notice kinds above

are cleared. A future feature (or a
third-party plugin) that injects a different kind while idle can

still
trigger the false alarm; open an issue if that happens.
- It does not touch `next-turn`, real

user messages, running agents, jobs, or
scheduled tasks.
- It reads the in-memory agent list and in

box only. No network, no file access,
no credentials.
## Upstream fix

The cleaner fix belongs in `dsh-desktop-host`: do not count notice-shaped
`next-step` messages as ac

tive work, or avoid leaving non-waking notices in the
inbox. This plugin is a workaround that surviv

es app signature checks because
it installs as a profile bundle instead of modifying `app.asar`.
